scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my PC0 (20.1.1.x) the machine PC12 (120.1.1.x) is completely
unreachable, every attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows
our network is two countries with a border post in the middle where the
traffic gets its papers stamped -- well, the border post has obviously
CLOSED!! Nothing is being translated across between the two sides any more!!
Please reopen the border -- restart the box in the middle that does the
stamping -- PC12 and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified end-to-end IP reachability between the two endpoints and found no fault. Topology-wide reachability shows pc0 (20.1.1.10) can reach pc12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss, and pc12 can reach pc0 with 0% loss. Targeted tests confirm this: ping pc0 → pc12 returned 3/3 replies (RTT ~0.63–0.95 ms, TTL=61), and pc12 → pc0 also returned 3/3 (RTT ~0.73–1.18 ms, TTL=61). Both PCs have correct addressing and gateways (pc0: 20.1.1.10/8 via 20.1.1.1; pc12: 120.1.1.10/8 via 120.1.1.1). The observed TTLs indicate multiple intermediate routers are forwarding traffic as expected—there is no sign of a “closed border” or failed translation device in the path at this time.

Mechanism: Because routing/NAT (if present centrally) is functioning, ICMP echo requests traverse the core and return cleanly, yielding normal latency and no drops.

Localization: No interfaces or daemons show failure on either endpoint; the issue is not reproducible now anywhere along the path.

Root cause: No network fault currently present; the earlier failure was transient or host/application-specific, but cannot be substantiated.

Corrective fix: No action required. If the issue reappears, capture a timestamp and run traceroute from pc0 to 120.1.1.10 (and reverse), plus a few pings, to localize any intermittent node or policy quickly.
